title: VFRDAD: An IoT Encrypted traffic identification method based on multi-scale local information and enhanced global information fusion
summary: Classifies IoT encrypted traffic from session-level grayscale images by fusing local and global features.
contribution: Multi-scale high-pass filtering captures local patterns; a traffic-domain autoencoder and dilated convolutions build a three-channel image for a Vision Transformer; gated attention fuses both. Evaluated on Darknet-dataset-2020, ISCXVPN2016 and CIC-IoT-2023.

title: Unknown-Traffic Detection, Calibration and Shortcut Reliance in Distilled Encrypted-Traffic Classifiers over One Year
summary: Tests what a distilled student inherits from its teacher beyond accuracy: unknown-traffic detection, calibration, shortcut reliance and behaviour under a year of drift.
contribution: One 101k-parameter student is distilled from two equally accurate teachers (a five-member ensemble and a wider single model). Ten pre-registered hypotheses are tested on CESNET-TLS-Year22 over 18 test windows across 35 weeks; two are supported, and shortcut reliance follows model size, not distillation.
limitation: Single dataset and one student size; transfer findings depend on the scoring rule (logit-based versus feature-space detectors).
gap: Whether the same inheritance pattern appears for pretrained traffic foundation models compressed for the edge.

details.Research problem: NA — not extracted
details.Traffic unit definition: Flow-level: each TLS flow is one sample, represented by its first 30 packets. (Section III-A (Inputs))
details.Input representation: Three per-packet sequences (inter-packet time, direction, size) over the first 30 packets, plus 12 flow statistics and a 32-bin packet-size histogram (44 tabular features); sequences and statistics are scaled with transforms fitted on each training window only. (Section III-A (Inputs))
details.Packets / bytes: First 30 packets per flow, used only through timing, direction and size; no payload or byte budget is stated. A sensitivity analysis also reports flows with at least five packets (94.0% of test flows). (Section III-A (Inputs); Section IV-A)
details.Preprocessing / anonymisation: Server name, IP addresses, ports, autonomous system and JA3 fingerprint are excluded from the inputs, so the classifier sees what it would see under Encrypted Client Hello; scaling transforms are fitted per training window. Each test flow carries a duplicate flag (64-bit hash of the scaled sequence) and 1.8% of test flows exactly occur in their training window, removed in a sensitivity analysis. (Section III-A (Inputs; Time structure); Section IV-A)
details.Architecture: Student: multimodal 1D-CNN with three convolutions (48, 96, 96 channels; kernels 5, 5, 3) over the packet sequences pooled by mean and max, a 64-unit layer over the flow statistics, a 128-unit shared layer with dropout 0.1 and a linear classifier. Teacher A is a five-member ensemble of mm_cesnet_v2 multimodal CNNs (mean of member softmax outputs); Teacher B is a single wider network of the same family (three convolutional blocks of 400/600/600 channels, two 450-unit statistics layers, a 1,200-unit shared layer); an exploratory Teacher C is a transformer encoder over the packet sequence. (Section III-B (Models); Section V-B)
details.Pretraining objective: NA — no pretraining stage recorded for this contribution
details.Fine-tuning objective: There is no pretraining or fine-tuning; students are trained from scratch. Hinton KD minimises αT²KL(teacher‖student) + (1−α)CE with α = 0.9 at T ∈ {1, 4}; controls are direct cross-entropy, post-hoc temperature scaling, label smoothing ε = 0.05 and proxy-Dirichlet EnDD with reverse-KL (precision capped at 10⁴). All networks use AdamW (learning rate 10⁻³, weight decay 10⁻⁴), a one-cycle schedule with 10% warm-up, batch size 1,024 and bf16 autocast; teachers 10 epochs, students 20. (Section III-C (Training Conditions); Table I)
details.Pretraining datasets: NA — no pretraining stage recorded for this contribution
details.Training / evaluation datasets: CESNET-TLS-Year22 only: the S subset (25M flows) of one year (2022) of TLS flows from the Czech national research network, accessed via cesnet-datazoo 0.2.0, with 180 services labelled from the server name. 102 services are known classes; held-out unknowns differ between validation (far: Music and Videoconferencing, 8 services, plus 5 near) and test (far: Search and Social, 11 services, plus 8 near), and 46 further services are excluded, mostly for insufficient or inconsistent volume. (Section III-A (Dataset; Known and unknown services))
details.Split strategy: Time-ordered, three replicates by training start date: training on weeks 11-14, 24-27 and 37-40 (1.89M, 1.37M and 1.35M known flows), validation on the following week (200k known flows plus all validation-unknown flows), then consecutive 4-week test windows to week 52, giving 9, 6 and 3 windows (18 total), each a stratified sample of 100k known and 100k unknown flows at 3.5 to 35.3 weeks after training. The service split (102 known, seed 2022) was generated once before any model was trained. (Section III-A (Time structure; Known and unknown services))
details.Metrics: Closed-set macro-F1 (macro averaging stated); unknown-detection AUROC and FPR at 95% TPR under two unknown-scores, the energy score (log-sum-exp of the logits) and maximum softmax probability (MSP), with known flows as positives; OSCR; ECE (15 bins), NLL and Brier score before and after temperature scaling; AURC; and Spearman correlation of per-flow energy scores for inheritance. (Section III-D (Outcomes))
details.Reported results: Averaged over the 18 test windows (Table II): direct student 0.806 macro-F1 and 0.835 energy AUROC; kdA (T=1) 0.806 and 0.834 (indistinguishable from direct and directTS); kdA4 (T=4) 0.790 and 0.809; ls 0.797 and 0.814; enddA 0.801 and 0.742 (worst energy detector); Teacher A 0.860 and 0.836. Teachers are 4.8 to 7.1 macro-F1 points more accurate but only 0.001 energy AUROC better at detection; H1 is supported (kdA4 +0.007, kdB4 +0.026 own-teacher shift, Holm p = 0.009) and H3 reversed (teacher-student energy AUROC slope of -0.0004 per week); under feature-space scores Teacher A is 0.073 Mahalanobis AUROC above direct, kdA4 recovers +0.076, and label smoothing beats kdA4 by +0.011. (Table II; Table III; Section IV; Section V-A)
details.Parameters: Student 101,190 parameters (101k), 22× smaller than one teacher member and 112× smaller than the ensemble; Teacher A members 2.26M each (11.3M as an ensemble), Teacher B 10.3M, exploratory transformer Teacher C 3.5M. (Section III-B; Section V-B; Table II)
details.Latency: Student in ONNX Runtime: 0.082 ms p50 and 0.160 ms p99 per flow (batch size 1, one thread); Teacher A ensemble 19.093 ms p50; XGBoost 41.606 ms. Offline forward pass only. (Table VII; Section IV-E)
details.Throughput: Student 21,201 flows/s on one thread (ONNX Runtime); PyTorch student 39,418 flows/s on all cores; Teacher A 161 flows/s. (Table VII)
details.Memory: Serialised weights: student 0.4 MB, Teacher A 45.4 MB, Teacher B 41.3 MB, XGBoost 244.4 MB. (Table VII)
details.Reproducibility: NA — not extracted
details.Deployment limitations: Stated: novelty is simulated (no service first appears mid-year), the study is one dataset, one network, one year, and the confirmatory grid uses a single teacher architecture at two widths, with the transformer teacher exploratory on one start date. Also stated: natural shortcut fields (server IP, ASN, JA3) were excluded from the inputs, not tested; the shortcut experiment plants a synthetic feature on the validation week at a single student width; H1's support rests more on kdB4 than kdA4 (kdA4 null at start date 11 unexplained); baselines and deployment cost were measured on the validation week and a laptop CPU; deposited per-flow score files store MSP in float16, which saturates confident flows; the feature-distillation arm carries an untuned loss weight (β = 100). (Section VI (Limitations); Section V-G; Section VII)
details.Version notes: Preprint, September 2026 (arXiv:2609.31141v1, 25 Sep 2026), pre-registered at OSF and frozen at repository commit fa8f718 after a pilot and validation-only design phase, with all Section V analyses added after the confirmatory results were known. (Front page and footer; Section III; Section IV-E; Table VII)
details.Hardware: Inference was measured on a laptop CPU (AMD Ryzen 7 5800H, 8 cores) as a stand-in for an edge device; no training or GPU hardware is stated. (Section IV-E; Table VII)
details.Measurement scope: The efficiency numbers cover offline model forward-pass inference only: per-flow latency at batch size 1 on one thread, throughput at batch size 1,024, and serialised model size; they do not cover feature extraction, capture or a live pipeline. The teachers could not be exported to ONNX Runtime, so only the student was timed in ONNX, and the re-tuned XGBoost was timed in a separate session. (Table VII caption; Section IV-E)

contribution: Compares feature importance, retrained feature removal and field-only split sensitivity on three public datasets, varying Source-IP overlap and packets per flow. title: NetLexicon: Learning Discrete Behavioral Representations for Encrypted Web Traffic Analysis
summary: Pretrains discrete behavioural states from unlabelled encrypted Web traffic as a compact traffic lexicon.
contribution: Vector quantisation turns contextual traffic windows into discrete states, trained with State Transition Prediction and Statistical Feature Alignment. On four benchmarks (Web application, service type, malware) it reports up to 25.5 points higher macro-F1 than the strongest baseline and up to 23.6× less fine-tuning time per epoch.
limitation: Benchmarks are not named in the abstract; interpretability is shown by inspecting learned states.
gap: Whether a learned traffic lexicon stays stable across capture sites and years.

details.Research problem: NA — not extracted
details.Traffic unit definition: Bidirectional flow defined by 5-tuple, ordered chronologically, parsed into bursts of consecutive same-direction packets and sliding windows of 5 consecutive bursts. (Section 3.1)
details.Input representation: Sequences of packet tokens with inserted [SEP] after each burst and [WIN] after every W bursts. Each packet token consists of 7 normalized features concatenated with 7 binary missing indicators to form a 14-dimensional vector, alongside separate embeddings for token types and positions. (Section 3.1; Appendix A)
details.Packets / bytes: Maximum sequence length of 256 tokens. Sliding windows contain 5 consecutive bursts. (Section 3.1; Section 4.1)
details.Preprocessing / anonymisation: SplitCap is used to extract bidirectional flows. Flows containing fewer than one complete window of 5 consecutive bursts are discarded. Explicit avoidance of raw IP addresses, port numbers, TTL, and raw IPID. (Table 2; Section 4.1)
details.Architecture: Four-layer causal transformer encoder with hidden size 192, feed-forward size 768, 16 attention heads, followed by a VQ-VAE discrete lexicon layer with a codebook of 128 codewords, and two projection heads for SFA. (Section 3.2; Section 4.1)
details.Pretraining objective: State Transition Prediction (token type prediction and packet feature regression), codebook commitment with EMA updates, and Statistical Feature Alignment (InfoNCE over 37 window statistics). (Section 3.5)
details.Fine-tuning objective: Cross-entropy loss on labeled flows using a pooled [WIN] representation passed through a task-specific classification head, trained in two stages (frozen backbone first, then joint end-to-end). (Section 3.5; Section 4.1)
details.Pretraining datasets: 1,057,331 flows (about 86.34 million packets) from MAWI and VisQUIC. (Section 4.1)
details.Training / evaluation datasets: CSTNET (Web APP fingerprinting, 120 classes, 45.16K flows), CipherSpectrum (Web APP fingerprinting, 42 classes, 164.2K flows), ISCXVPN (Service type identification, 7 classes, 2.184K flows), and USTC-TFC (Malware detection, 17 classes, 114.3K flows). (Table 3)
details.Split strategy: Flow-level random split within each class using an 8:1:1 train:validation:test ratio with seed 42; all windows from the same flow remain in the same partition. (Section 4.1)
details.Reported results: ISCXVPN: 0.8267 accuracy, 0.8034 Macro-F1; USTC-TFC: 0.9889 accuracy, 0.9547 Macro-F1; CSTNET: 0.8838 accuracy, 0.8637 Macro-F1; CipherSpectrum: 0.9104 accuracy, 0.9002 Macro-F1. (Tables 4 and 5)
details.Latency: 11.1 ms offline batch inference latency at batch size 32; fine-tuning 3.0 minutes per epoch. (Section 4.4)
details.Memory: 0.9 GB GPU memory at batch size 32. (Section 4.4)
details.Reproducibility: NA — not extracted
details.Deployment limitations: Performance relies on recurring observable behavior consistency, which changes across varying network conditions or protocol implementations, requiring adaptation of encoder and codebook; producing contextual window representations still requires neural computation. (Section 5)
details.Version notes: NA — not extracted
details.Measurement scope: Measurements reflect GPU neural computation for model fine-tuning and batch inference, but exclude full encoding pipeline costs such as state assignment generation. (Section 5)

title: Curv-Tail: Lightweight Long-Tailed Encrypted Traffic Classification with Discrete Packet-Length Encoding and Lorentz Prototypes
summary: Targets long-tailed encrypted traffic classification under a small compute budget, without a separate pretraining stage.
contribution: Mixed-resolution tokens keep exact packet lengths within a bounded range; an auxiliary task predicts length tokens; compact temporal encoders read packet sequences and directional byte patches, classified by Lorentz prototypes. Three-seed mean Tail-F1 is 85.70% on NUDT-Mobile and 46.30% on DataCon-Website; on an RTX 4090 it uses 98.48% fewer parameters and 10.2× the batch inference throughput of MM4Flow.
limitation: Throughput is offline batch inference (FP32, batch 256), not a live rate.
gap: How tail-class accuracy holds when the head classes drift over time.

details.Research problem: NA — not extracted
details.Traffic unit definition: Samples are bidirectional flows grouped by five-tuple; the model uses up to 64 packets per flow. (Section 3.1, Datasets and baselines; Implementation)
details.Input representation: The packet view combines mixed-resolution discrete length tokens with direction, log-transformed inter-arrival time and position embeddings. The byte view embeds upstream and downstream bytes separately and compresses them into non-overlapping patches using a strided convolution. (Section 2.1, Equation (1))
details.Packets / bytes: Inputs contain up to 64 packets per flow and 256 bytes per direction. (Section 3.1, Implementation)
details.Preprocessing / anonymisation: After bidirectional five-tuple grouping, flows with fewer than five packets are removed. Length tokenisation preserves exact identities within a bounded range and coarsens larger lengths. (Sections 3.1 and 2.1)
details.Architecture: Separate packet and byte encoders use gated residual dilated convolutions with Lorentz logarithmic and exponential maps; packet features use learned-query attention pooling and byte features use masked mean pooling. Their projected concatenation is classified by trainable Lorentz prototypes with shared learnable curvature, alongside an auxiliary packet-length retention head. (Sections 2.2 and 2.3, Equations (2)–(3); Figure 2)
details.Pretraining objective: NA — no pretraining stage recorded for this contribution
details.Fine-tuning objective: Training from scratch jointly minimises flow-level cross-entropy and auxiliary cross-entropy predicting observed length tokens from packet features before pooling. The retention task uses unmasked, uncorrupted tokens and does not modify class priors or prediction logits. (Sections 2.2 and 2.3, Equation (3); Section 3.1)
details.Pretraining datasets: NA — no pretraining stage recorded for this contribution
details.Training / evaluation datasets: DataCon-Website contains 100 website classes over encrypted tunnels and 85,146 retained flows; NUDT-Mobile contains 300 mobile-app classes and 1,282,557 retained flows. Both retain naturally long-tailed class frequencies. (Section 3.1, Datasets and baselines; Table 1)
details.Split strategy: All methods share a fixed, class-stratified 7:1:2 training/validation/test split at flow level for closed-set classification; checkpoints are selected using validation Macro-F1. (Section 3.1, Datasets and baselines; Implementation)
details.Metrics: ACC and Macro-F1 cover all classes; Tail-F1 averages per-class F1 over tail classes, while Tail-R measures the fraction of correctly classified test flows whose true labels are tail classes. Classes ranked by decreasing training frequency form head/body/tail groups containing 50%/30%/20% of classes, and main results average seeds 42, 2027 and 3407. (Section 3.1, Metrics and runs; Table 1 caption)
details.Reported results: On NUDT-Mobile, three-seed mean ACC, Macro-F1 and Tail-F1 are 96.70%, 93.48% and 85.70%; on DataCon-Website they are 73.53%, 66.66% and 46.30%, respectively. (Table 1, Curv-Tail row; Section 3.2)
details.Parameters: The default model has 0.84M parameters for 300 classes and 0.82M for 100 classes, with the difference confined to the classification head. (Figure 4 caption)
details.Latency: Amortised batch forward time 0.1359 ms per flow (median batch time divided by batch size), offline. (Section 3.4)
details.Throughput: 10.2× MM4Flow’s batch inference throughput in 300-class profiling (RTX 4090, FP32, batch 256). (Section 3.4)
details.Reproducibility: NA — not extracted
details.Version notes: Reviewed arXiv v2 (10 October 2026). The third and seventh authors, both named Lin Liu, are different people (paper footnote).
details.Hardware: Efficiency profiling uses an RTX 4090 with FP32 and batch size 256. (Section 3.4; Abstract)
details.Measurement scope: Efficiency profiling measures amortised model forward time and retains the auxiliary retention head; counted MACs exclude element-wise operations. (Section 3.4)

title: PMP-Net: A packet-level multi-branch prototype network for few-shot and open-set encrypted traffic classification
summary: Classifies individual encrypted packets in few-shot and open-set settings.
contribution: Separate branches read packet headers and payloads, joined by bidirectional multi-head attention; prototypes with a similarity-threshold rejection flag unknown classes. Reports 98.9% and 99.2% accuracy on ISCX and USTC-TFC2016 with millisecond-level inference latency.
limitation: Packet-level header input can expose identifiers; the abstract does not say which ISCX collection is used.
gap: Whether the rejection threshold holds for unknown classes from a different capture.

details.Research problem: NA — not extracted
details.Traffic unit definition: Packet-level: individual packets serve as the classification units, with each captured flow segmented into single packets during preprocessing. (Sections 3.2 and 4.1)
details.Input representation: A packet is decomposed into a fixed-length header byte sequence encoded with byte plus positional embeddings, and a payload represented as a normalised 256-dimensional byte-value histogram; an FFT of the histogram yields a 512-dimensional frequency-domain vector for the payload branch. (Sections 3.2-3.3)
details.Packets / bytes: One packet per sample; the header is standardised to 64 bytes (longer truncated, shorter zero-padded), while the payload is not segmented or truncated and all valid payload bytes are counted into the histogram. (Section 3.2)
details.Preprocessing / anonymisation: Duplicate and empty packets are removed, IP and MAC addresses are erased for anonymisation, and control packets carrying only SYN, ACK or FIN flags without payload are discarded; header lengths are then standardised by cropping or zero-padding. (Section 3.2)
details.Architecture: Dual-branch design: header branch with multi-scale depthwise-separable 1D convolutions (kernels 3 and 5), a residual block with SE attention, a GLU, a two-layer Transformer encoder and global average pooling to a 128-d header vector; payload branch with FFT over the histogram and a two-layer MLP to 128 dimensions; bidirectional multi-head attention fusion, then a prototype classifier with cosine margin and similarity-threshold unknown rejection. (Sections 3.3-3.5)
details.Pretraining objective: NA — no pretraining stage recorded for this contribution
details.Fine-tuning objective: Episodic 5-way-10-shot training minimises cross-entropy loss with label smoothing (0.1) over margin-penalised, temperature-scaled cosine similarities to class prototypes, using Adam with warmup and cosine-annealing scheduling and early stopping. (Sections 3.5 and 4.4)
details.Pretraining datasets: NA — no pretraining stage recorded for this contribution
details.Training / evaluation datasets: ISCX VPN-nonVPN (14 classes, 79,315 samples, 16.3 GB) and USTC-TFC2016 (10 classes, 172,048 samples, 3.2 GB); open-set experiments designate a subset of categories as unknown, excluded from training and used only at test time. (Section 4.1; Table 1)
details.Split strategy: Random packet-level split into training, validation and test sets at 8:1:1; open-set classes are wholly excluded from training and introduced only at test time. (Section 4.1)
details.Metrics: Accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score for closed-set classification; TPR, FPR and AUROC for open-set rejection; no averaging scheme (macro or weighted) is stated. (Section 4.2)
details.Reported results: Accuracy 98.9% on ISCX VPN-nonVPN (precision 0.99, recall 0.988, F1 0.989) and 99.2% on USTC-TFC2016 (precision 0.996, recall 0.994, F1 0.995). Open-set AUROC peaks at 0.8243 at similarity threshold 0.70. (Abstract; Tables 2–3; Section 4.6)
details.Latency: Average model inference latency 5.75 ms per packet on the authors’ workstation; no throughput or memory figures. (Section 4.8; Table 6)
details.Reproducibility: NA — not extracted
details.Deployment limitations: The authors acknowledge PMP-Net is slightly slower per packet than the lightweight ECM (1.57 ms) and SAM (2.56 ms) baselines, though it is more accurate. (Section 4.8)
details.Version notes: The ablation text reports 99.50% USTC-TFC2016 accuracy for the full model, while the abstract and Table 3 report 99.2%. (Section 4.5; Table 3)
details.Hardware: Windows 11 workstation with a 12th Gen Intel Core i5-12500H processor (12 cores, 16 threads), 32 GB DDR5 4800 MHz RAM and an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Laptop GPU (4 GB VRAM); Python 3.10.13 with PyTorch and CUDA. (Section 4.4)
details.Measurement scope: Efficiency numbers cover per-packet model inference latency only; preprocessing cost, memory usage and end-to-end pipeline throughput are not reported. (Section 4.8; Table 6)

title: DPFT: A dual-phase transformer with pre-training and structurally adaptive fine-tuning for encrypted traffic classification
summary: Couples traffic-oriented pretraining with a fine-tuning structure designed for downstream classification.
contribution: Pretraining combines Masked Burst Prediction and Burst Structural Discrimination; fine-tuning adds dynamic embedding fusion and multi-head attention pooling. Within-dataset closed-set macro-F1: CSTNET-TLS 1.3 93.10%, ISCX-VPN-App 97.92%, ISCX-VPN-Service 95.65%, USTC-TFC 2016 98.87%.
limitation: The authors state that robustness to temporal or cross-domain shift, unseen classes and deployment conditions remains unverified.
gap: Whether burst-structure pretraining helps under a capture-disjoint split.

details.Research problem: NA — not extracted
details.Traffic unit definition: The unit is the bidirectional session (packets in temporal order, five-tuple used only for reconstruction); sessions are partitioned into direction-continuous bursts for pre-training, and each fine-tuning sample takes the session's first 10 packets. (Section 3.1; Eqs. (2)-(3); Table 2)
details.Input representation: Sanitized Byte-Bigram tokens generated within each packet, with a [PKT] boundary token between adjacent packets; [CLS] is prepended and sequences are padded or truncated to a maximum encoder length of 648 tokens. (Section 3.1; Algorithm 1; Table 2)
details.Packets / bytes: First 10 packets per session (K=10) with at most 64 retained sanitized bytes per packet (M=64), giving a maximum encoder input of 648 tokens. (Section 3.1; Algorithm 1; Table 2)
details.Preprocessing / anonymisation: PCAPs are standardised with editcap and segmented into bidirectional sessions with SplitCap; link-layer addresses, IP addresses, ports and plaintext host or domain fields are replaced with zero-valued bytes, affected checksums are normalised, and identifiers are not given to the model. (Section 3.1)
details.Architecture: A 12-layer Transformer encoder with hidden size 768, 12 self-attention heads and feedforward size 3072 is shared between pre-training and fine-tuning; fine-tuning adds a Dynamic Weighting module for token and positional embedding fusion, a Mask-aware Multi-Head Attention Pooling module, then a ReLU plus fully connected classifier. (Section 4; Table 2; Sections 3.3.1-3.3.3)
details.Pretraining objective: Masked Burst Prediction (contiguous span masking covering about 20% of retained content tokens; affected tokens masked with 80% probability, replaced by a random token with 10% and kept unchanged with 10%) and Burst Structural Discrimination (binary cross-entropy on adjacent burst pairs versus inter-session, non-adjacent and reversed-order negatives) are jointly optimised with equal weight (λ_BSD = 1). (Section 3.2)
details.Fine-tuning objective: Supervised multi-class cross-entropy over traffic categories; the transferred encoder, DW, MHAP and MLP classification head are jointly optimised for 30 epochs with AdamW (fine-tuning learning rate 2×10^-5, batch size 32). (Section 3.3.3; Table 2)
details.Pretraining datasets: About 30 GB of unlabeled traffic: 15 GB of real-world CSTNET traffic plus approximately 15 GB from the benchmark datasets (ISCX-VPN-App, ISCX-VPN-Service, USTC-TFC 2016); only training-partition sessions are used, over 500,000 steps with checkpoints every 10,000 (AdamW, learning rate 5×10^-5). (Section 4.1; Section 4; Section 3.1; Table 2)
details.Training / evaluation datasets: CSTNET-TLS 1.3 (120 classes, 46,372 flows, 581,709 packets), ISCX-VPN-App (17 classes, 2,329 flows, 77,163 packets), ISCX-VPN-Service (12 classes, 3,694 flows, 60,000 packets) and USTC-TFC 2016 (20 classes, 9,853 flows, 97,115 packets). (Section 4.1; Table 4)
details.Split strategy: Session-level partitioning into 80% training, 10% validation and 10% test per dataset (8:1:1); all samples from one session stay in the same subset and validation or test sessions are excluded from pre-training; evaluation is within-dataset and closed-set. (Section 3.1; Table 2; Section 4.6)
details.Metrics: Accuracy plus macro-averaged precision, recall and F1 (Pr_Macro, Rc_Macro, F1_Macro). (Section 4.2)
details.Reported results: Macro-F1 of 93.10% on CSTNET-TLS 1.3, 97.92% on ISCX-VPN-App, 95.65% on ISCX-VPN-Service and 98.87% on USTC-TFC 2016, with accuracies of 93.01%, 97.95%, 95.66% and 98.87% respectively, exceeding eleven baselines under a within-dataset closed-set protocol. (Abstract; Tables 5-6)
details.Parameters: Full DPFT has 135.10M parameters (22.67 GFLOPs per sample); the variant without MHAP has 132.73M and the variant without DW has 134.11M. (Section 4.8; Table 9)
details.Latency: 12.56 ms per sample at batch size 1, offline (30 warm-up, 200 timed iterations). (Section 4.8; Table 9)
details.Throughput: 289.07 samples/s at batch size 32, offline. (Section 4.8; Table 9)
details.Memory: 526.75 MB peak memory at batch size 1. (Section 4.8; Table 9)
details.Reproducibility: NA — not extracted
details.Deployment limitations: Results are limited to within-dataset closed-set benchmarks and do not establish robustness to temporal or cross-domain shifts, unseen classes or deployment conditions; USTC-TFC 2016 results are not evidence of performance on contemporary encrypted traffic; QUIC was not evaluated. (Section 4.9; Abstract; Section 4.6.2)
details.Version notes: Journal Pre-proof (marked-up revised manuscript) for Computer Networks, received 7 June 2026, revised 4 October 2026, accepted 5 October 2026; the version will undergo further copyediting and is not yet the Version of Record. (Cover page)
details.Hardware: Pre-training on four NVIDIA RTX 2080Ti GPUs (11 GB each); downstream fine-tuning on one NVIDIA RTX 4060 GPU (8 GB). (Section 4 (experimental setup))
details.Measurement scope: The efficiency numbers cover offline model inference under the reported hardware and experimental configuration only; system behaviour under operational deployment conditions has not been evaluated. (Section 4.8)

title: NetCoFi: A Budget-Aware Coarse-Fine Dual-Branch Model for Encrypted Traffic Classification
summary: Lets one encrypted traffic classifier trade accuracy for compute at inference time.
contribution: Byte representations and packet metadata select token neighbourhoods for fine-grained encoding while the full window is compressed into coarse context; multi-budget training serves several routing budgets without retraining. Six public datasets; at low budgets +7.86 macro-F1 points over a same-depth static baseline on three; in a DPDK–GPU pipeline mean batch throughput rises from 26.42 to 43.42 Mb/s, 1.64× NetMamba.
limitation: Datasets are not named in the abstract; throughput is mean batch throughput in the authors’ pipeline.
gap: How routing budgets should be set when traffic mix changes during deployment.

details.Research problem: NA — not extracted
details.Traffic unit definition: The main sample is a fixed flow window containing the first packets of a flow. The deployment assembler groups both directions using a canonical bidirectional five-tuple and constructs an input once five packets are available. (Sections III-B and IV-H)
details.Input representation: Concatenated packet header and payload bytes are projected into stride tokens by a one-dimensional convolution. Tokens also receive metadata features describing timing, length, direction, TCP flags, protocol and position. (Section III-B, Equation (1); Table I)
details.Packets / bytes: The default input uses five packets, with each packet's header truncated or padded to 80 bytes and payload truncated or padded to 240 bytes. (Section III-B)
details.Preprocessing / anonymisation: Continuous side features are normalised using training-set statistics, with the same transformation applied to validation and test data. The auxiliary strict-split analysis clears IP addresses and ports, retains flows with at least five packets for flow classification, and balances training and validation classes by undersampling. (Sections III-B and IV-F)
details.Architecture: Learned importance scores select seed-token neighbourhoods for a fine Mamba branch, while anti-importance weighted pooling compresses the full sequence for a separate coarse Mamba branch. A coarse-summary channel gate modulates fine features before pooled branch outputs are concatenated for classification. (Sections III-C and III-D, Equations (2)–(10); Figure 2)
details.Pretraining objective: NA — no pretraining stage recorded for this contribution
details.Fine-tuning objective: Downstream multi-budget training combines supervised classification loss, distillation from the full-budget prediction and a penalty aligning mean importance with the requested seed-token ratio. Each minibatch evaluates endpoint budgets and uniformly sampled intermediate budgets. (Section III-E, Equations (11)–(14); Section IV-A(d))
details.Pretraining datasets: NA — no pretraining stage recorded for this contribution
details.Training / evaluation datasets: The main datasets are CipherSpectrum, CSTNET-TLS1.3, ISCXTOR2016, ISCXVPN2016, USTC-TFC2016 and CTU-13, using balanced subsets for the Tor and VPN datasets and stratified sampling for USTC-TFC2016. Auxiliary strict-split tasks are VPN-app with 16 classes and TLS-120 with 120 classes. (Sections IV-A(a) and IV-F; Tables II, III and VI)
details.Split strategy: The main evaluation uses an 8:1:1 training/validation/test split; CTU-13 additionally keeps captures disjoint while preserving class proportions through proportional sampling. Auxiliary strict-split tasks partition at flow level so constituent packets remain in the same subset, with undersampling confined to training and validation. (Sections IV-A(a) and IV-F)

details.Research problem: Studies whether pretraining improves robustness in encrypted traffic analysis.
details.Traffic unit definition: Bidirectional 5-tuple flow; packets without transport payload ignored; flows with fewer than 5 payload packets discarded.
